subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should adding the first `agents.list` entry be allowed to change the default agent by list order, or should OpenClaw require/warn about an explicit default when existing implicit `main` state would be displaced?
rationale: Current main documents first-entry fallback, but the issue shows session continuity, message routing, and security risk when users add a specialized ACP agent; changing the fallback or only warning both carry compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Gate With Explicit Default
options.body: Keep runtime parsing compatible, but make config/setup/doctor flows warn or fail when the first non-empty `agents.list` has no explicit default and existing `main` state would be displaced.

options.title: Warn Only
options.body: Preserve first-entry fallback everywhere and add high-visibility warnings plus docs/doctor guidance for users adding their first listed agent.

options.title: Auto-Preserve Main
options.body: Materialize or promote `main` as default when `main` state exists, protecting continuity while changing first-entry-only config meaning.

recommendation.title: Gate With Explicit Default
recommendation.body: Keep runtime parsing compatible, but make config/setup/doctor flows warn or fail when the first non-empty `agents.list` has no explicit default and existing `main` state would be displaced.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the multi-agent routing/default behavior points to the original routing work and adjacent route-cache maintenance.
